title: Farmers and Shiv Sena UBT protest for drought relief in Washim
seoTitle: Washim farmers protest for drought relief

tea.why: Farmers and Shiv Sena (UBT) protested against inadequate drought relief and crop destruction caused by a lack of rain.
tea.want: They demanded compensation of Rs 1 lakh per hectare, settlement of crop insurance claims, and remunerative prices.
tea.changed: Oct 30: Police detained MLA Nitin Deshmukh and several protesters before releasing them at 5 pm.

summary: On October 30, 2026, hundreds of farmers and Shiv Sena (UBT) members, led by MLA Nitin Deshmukh, gathered at the Vanoja interchange in Washim district to march toward the Samruddhi Expressway. The demonstration aimed to block traffic and demand increased drought relief, specifically compensation of Rs 1 lakh per hectare, faster crop insurance settlements, and better produce prices, as participants stated that kharif crops had been ruined by dry conditions. Authorities deployed approximately 1,500 police personnel and State Reserve Police Force units, having previously denied permission for the expressway agitation. Police halted the march, leading to scuffles and the eventual detention of Deshmukh and other participants, who were later released in the evening.
demands: Compensation of Rs 1 lakh per hectare for drought-hit farmers
Immediate settlement of crop insurance claims
response: Police deployed nearly 1,500 personnel and SRPF units, denied permission for the protest, blocked demonstrators from reaching the expressway, and detained MLA Nitin Deshmukh along with other participants before releasing them later that evening.

crowd.text: Over 10,000 farmers from across Vidarbha took part in the protest, according to MLA Nitin Deshmukh.

updates.text: Shiv Sena (UBT) members and farmers marched toward the Samruddhi Expressway in Washim to protest over drought relief.
Police deployed 1,500 personnel and detained MLA Nitin Deshmukh and participants before releasing them at 5 pm.

conflicts: Organisers claimed over 10,000 farmers participated, while official reports noted hundreds of party workers and farmers heading toward the expressway.
